W.note: Syllables are 5-7-5 (First snow on the ridge / the lens holds, wind running through / and the cloud stays still), and the lens cloud is an accurate lenticular evocation, though it is never named; the stillness-against-wind turn is quiet and effective.

X.note: Syllables are 5-7-5 (Rare cloud, mother-pearl / blooms where the sky holds no sun, / gone before the name), mother-of-pearl accurately evokes nacreous clouds, and 'gone before the name' gives the rarity a strong closing turn, though the opening 'Rare cloud' is a bit plain.

Y.note: Syllables are 4-7-4 (Midwinter ridge: is 4, wind runs through a lens of cloud is 7, that does not move is 4), so it misses 5-7-5; it is a faithful lenticular image but reuses W's wind, lens and ridge almost word for word and ends flatly.

Z.note: Syllables are 5-7-5 (Night's edge, pearl-thin cloud / lit from beneath by the sun, / seen by no one else), and lit from below after sunset is the true mechanism of nacreous clouds, with 'seen by no one else' giving a lonely, earned turn.
